mechanism_narrative: A month-over-month decline in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) signals an easing monetary policy, which reduces discount rates for equity valuation and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: The 5-day forward returns show no positive correlation with the month-over-month change in FEDFUNDS (Rank IC < 0.03) over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate above 4.0% indicates a restrictive monetary policy, which increases discount rates and reduces equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are not significantly negative when FEDFUNDS > 4.0% (t-test p > 0.05) or Rank IC < -0.03 over any 2-year window.

mechanism_narrative: The negative impact of rising federal funds rates (FEDFUNDS) on equity returns is amplified when core inflation (CPIAUCSL) exceeds 3.5%, as high inflation signals persistent monetary tightening and economic uncertainty.
failure_condition: The negative return signal from the interaction (FEDFUNDS rising and CPIAUCSL YoY > 3.5%) fails to materialize in > 60% of cases (i.e., 20-day returns are positive in > 60% of triggered instances) or Rank IC < -0.03 over any 2-year window.

mechanism_narrative: In a tight labor market (unemployment rate below 4.0%), the risk of wage-driven inflation and subsequent monetary tightening leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: In periods when UNRATE < 4.0%, the 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) or the Rank IC is below -0.03 over any 3-year window.

mechanism_narrative: A housing starts level below 1500 thousand units signals weak consumer demand, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: When HOUST < 1500.0, the 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) or Rank IC < -0.03 over any 2-year window.

mechanism_narrative: A month-over-month decline in industrial production (INDPRO) signals a contraction in the real economy, reducing corporate earnings growth expectations and driving negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward returns show no negative correlation with the month-over-month change in INDPRO (Rank IC > -0.03) over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: The simultaneous decline in housing starts (HOUST) below 1500 thousand units and real personal consumption (RSAFS) below 750 billion dollars indicates a broad-based weakness in consumer demand, which reduces corporate revenue growth prospects and drives negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The negative return signal from the interaction (HOUST < 1500 and RSAFS < 750000) fails to materialize in > 60% of cases (i.e., 20-day returns are positive in > 60% of triggered instances) or Rank IC < -0.03 over any 2-year window.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion phase (when quarterly GDP growth is positive but below 2.0%), the economy is approaching a peak, increasing the risk of a recession and leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: In periods of late-cycle expansion (GDPC1 quarterly growth between 0.0% and 2.0%), the 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) or Rank IC < -0.03 over any 3-year window.
